findings.title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with wrong arity will not compile
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only method with that name defined in the parent class UsernamePasswordForm is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, which requires a UserModel parameter. There is no no-arg overload anywhere in the diff. This is a method signature mismatch that will fail to compile, breaking the entire build (and therefore all the new tests added in this PR as well).

findings.title: fillContextForm no longer called for anonymous/new login, breaking normal passkeys conditional UI
findings.body: The new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` helper returns true only when `user != null`. In `authenticate()`, the call `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is now used (unconditionally, replacing the previous `else`-branch-only check) to decide whether to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)`. Previously, this fill happened precisely when `context.getUser() == null` (i.e. during a fresh/anonymous login, to populate the conditional-UI webauthn attributes on the initial challenge). With the new condition requiring a non-null user, the webauthn/conditional-UI attributes will no longer be set for normal (non-reauthentication) logins where no user has been identified yet, which is the primary passkeys use case. This directly contradicts the assertions in the already-existing/updated tests (e.g. PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey) that still expect the webauthn form element to be present on the initial, unauthenticated login page.

findings.title: challenge(context, error, field) stops refilling webauthn data for anonymous users on error
findings.body: The overridden `challenge(AuthenticationFlowContext, String, String)` previously called `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `context.getUser() == null` (i.e. to keep the webauthn/passkeys UI available on the error page shown after an invalid username or an invalid password attempt where the user was never set in the auth context). It now uses `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which requires `user != null` and will therefore be false in exactly that anonymous-user error scenario. As a result, after a failed login attempt where the user isn't set in the auth context (e.g. wrong password for a non-reauthenticated session, where context.setUser() is only invoked on success), the webauthn conditional-UI attributes are no longer populated on the retry/error page, even though this scenario is explicitly asserted to still show the webauthn form in the updated test `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey`.

findings.title: Unused import left after replacing assertThrows usages
findings.body: The import `org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException` is no longer used anywhere in this file after the two `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` calls in `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` were replaced with `MatcherAssert.assertThat(..., Matchers.notNullValue())`. This leaves a dead/unused import that should be removed.
